isBasedOn.name: Verification as Identity: Accountability, Personhood and the Scarcity of Verification in the Agent Economy

abstract: The Article treats identity as a linkage rule that maps agent instances to records, shows that the rule's error rates set an agent's capacity to answer for harm, and derives the standing at which a principal's exposure falls to zero, with two regimes of failure: a cliff, in which the agent exits and the injured party recovers nothing, and graceful degradation, in which the agent stays and pays what it can. It extends the model to strategic claimants, partial inheritance, correlated harm, entry cost, verifier incentives and sponsorship chains. Two registered tests used a prompted language model with no stake, and the first failed on a specification error that the Article corrects. A descriptive study of 1,156 feedback events in the ERC-8004 registries finds almost no evidence attached and no consequence.
